question: A regular hexagonal prism is cut by an oblique plane. The true shape of the section is best obtained by which method?
options: Auxiliary view projection perpendicular to the cutting plane
Rotating the cutting plane to align with the principal plane
Direct measurement from the front elevation
Rabatment of the section onto the cutting plane

question: When drawing an isometric projection of a sphere of diameter 60 mm, what is the correct isometric diameter to use?
options: 60 mm

question: A cone resting on its base is cut by a plane parallel to its slant side. The resulting conic section is a:
options: Ellipse
Hyperbola
Parabola
Circle

question: In orthographic projection, the angle between the reference line XY and the true length line in a rabatment construction represents which angle?
options: The angle of inclination of the line to the horizontal plane
The angle of inclination of the line to the vertical plane
The angle between the cutting plane and the principal plane
The dihedral angle between the two projection planes

question: To find the true length of a skew line in space using descriptive geometry, the most direct single-step method is:
options: Draw an auxiliary view with the projection direction parallel to the line
Draw an auxiliary view with the projection direction perpendicular to the line
Rotate the line until it is parallel to the frontal plane
Project the line onto an oblique plane

question: The involute of a circle of radius r is generated by unwinding a taut string. The normal to any point on the involute is always:
options: Tangent to the base circle at the point of unwinding
Perpendicular to the base circle radius
Parallel to the initial tangent point
Directed toward the center of the base circle

question: A right circular cylinder is intersected by another cylinder of equal diameter with their axes at right angles and intersecting. The curve of interpenetration at the top view appears as:
options: An ellipse
A straight line
Two straight lines crossing at 90°
A true circle

question: In third-angle orthographic projection, which statement correctly describes the position of views?
options: The plan is placed below the front elevation and the side view is placed on the opposite side from which it is viewed
The plan is placed above the front elevation and the side view is placed on the same side from which it is viewed
The plan is placed below and the side view is on the same side from which it is viewed
The plan is placed above and the side view is on the opposite side from which it is viewed

question: The pitch of a helix is defined as:
options: The diameter of the cylinder on which the helix is drawn
The axial distance advanced in one complete revolution
The angle the helix makes with the axis of the cylinder
The length of one complete turn of the helix

question: When developing the lateral surface of an oblique cone by triangulation, the key step that distinguishes it from a right cone development is:
options: Using the slant height as the true length for all generators
Finding the true length of each individual generator before plotting
Dividing the base circle into equal parts and using chord lengths
Constructing a series of auxiliary planes through the apex

question: In a sectional assembly drawing, which of the following components should NOT be shown in section (i.e., left unhatched) when cut longitudinally?
options: Hollow cylindrical housing
Solid shaft
End plate
Bearing housing

question: A point P is 40 mm above the HP and 30 mm in front of the VP. Its front view (elevation) distance from XY is:
options: 30 mm
40 mm
50 mm
70 mm

question: The eccentricity of a conic section drawn using the focus-directrix method is defined as the ratio of:
options: The distance from the focus to the directrix divided by the distance from the vertex to the focus
The distance of the point from the focus to its perpendicular distance from the directrix
The semi-major axis to the semi-minor axis
The distance between the two foci to the length of the major axis

question: An auxiliary elevation is projected from the plan onto an auxiliary vertical plane inclined at 45° to the VP. This view is primarily used to show the true shape of a surface that is inclined to:
options: Both the HP and the VP
The HP only
The VP only
Neither the HP nor the VP

question: When constructing an Archimedean spiral, if the greatest radius is 90 mm and the spiral completes one revolution, the radius increases by what uniform amount for each 30° of rotation?
options: 9 mm
7.5 mm
10 mm
6 mm
